title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
description: Given an integer array `nums`, return the length of its longest **strictly increasing** subsequence. A subsequence keeps the original order but may skip elements.

examples.explanation: Equal values are not strictly increasing.

hints: Let dp[i] be the longest increasing subsequence that ends exactly at index i.
dp[i] = 1 + max(dp[j]) over earlier j with nums[j] < nums[i]. That gives O(n^2).
For O(n log n), keep an array where tails[k] is the smallest possible last value of an increasing subsequence of length k+1, and binary search where each number goes.

solution.explanation: Maintain a sorted list 'tails' where tails[k] is the smallest tail of any increasing subsequence of length k+1. For each number, binary search the first tail that is not smaller (strict increase) and replace it, or append if the number exceeds all tails. The list length is the answer. That is O(n log n) time and O(n) space; the simple dp[i] approach is O(n^2).
